mark-ring.note: The lighter half of the mark's source pair. Not consumed directly as a UI fill: its hue drives the dark-mode primary-container and the active-nav tone.

primary-light.note: The brand, the only hue that acts, and the 5G NR identity. The mark's 45-degree tail used literally.

primary-container-light.note: The tonal block carrying primary-flavored content: tonal buttons, the active nav pill, informational banners, in-progress rows.

lte-light.note: The 4G LTE identity and nothing else. Hue 296 because the mark forces blue to mean the primary radio. It never acts.

lte-container-light.note: LTE carrier tiles, LTE aggregation segments, the LTE identity chip, the Active MIMO tile.

uplink-light.note: Counts, upload direction, minor accents. Hue 200 clears 40 degrees from every functional hue. It never acts.

uplink-container-light.note: The carrier-count tile and the upload leg of a paired readout.

success-light.note: Healthy: connected, service active, save succeeded, profile applied. Always paired with a check glyph.

warning-light.note: Degraded: weak signal, searching, limited service, no SIM. Retuned down to L 0.585 in light because the old amber failed AA on a white card.

destructive-light.note: Failed or irreversible: disconnected, apply failed, no service, reboot dialogs.

background-light.note: The page background. Tinted toward the mark's hue 258 like every neutral in the system.

surface-light.note: Cards, dialogs, popovers. The step a card sits on.

surface-container-light.note: Inner tiles, metric row pills, input fills, the sidebar rail. Recesses in light, lifts in dark.

surface-container-high-light.note: Muted chips, deliberately-off states, glyph discs on neutral tiles.

on-surface-variant-light.note: Descriptions, labels, eyebrows, row keys, inactive nav.

outline-light.note: Input strokes and genuine table rules only. Never a card border.

success-on-surface-light.note: Tinted text on a plain card where no container is used — the fifth of the five functional tokens each role ships. Never crossed with `-container` ink.

warning-on-surface-light.note: Tinted text on a plain card where no container is used. Measures ~1.01:1 against success-on-surface — same luminance, hue only — so any tinted metric value also carries an sr-only quality word.

destructive-on-surface-light.note: Tinted text on a plain card where no container is used.

info-light.note: Not a fifth hue — a byte-identical alias of `primary-light`, per the Info-Is-Brand Rule. "In progress" renders as the brand's own tonal container; an info chip differs from a primary button by shape and glyph only, never by owning a second blue.

chart-nr-light.note: Alias of primary-light, one hue per radio family so a color learned on one card holds on the next. Never the numbered --chart-1..6, which are byte-identical across themes and don't separate NR from LTE under a color-vision deficiency.

chart-lte-light.note: Alias of lte-light, one hue per radio family.

chart-threshold-light.note: Alias of warning-light. Dashed, low-opacity threshold guide lines only.

display.purpose: The h1 at the top of every feature page, followed by a muted description. One per route.

headline.purpose: Large tile values, state-screen labels, section headings inside a hero card.

title.purpose: The card title on converted surfaces. CardTitle itself ships only leading-none font-semibold and takes its size from the call site.

body.purpose: Descriptions, prose, card copy, table cells. leading-relaxed and text-pretty on any paragraph over one line.

row.purpose: Keys and values on a glance card's pill rows. The 20px line box is load-bearing: it holds the row at exactly 40px so its skeleton keeps matching. Never used outside a dense metric row.

label.purpose: Chips, table headers, button text, form labels, tile eyebrows. 11px with tracking-wider for sidebar section labels.

numeric.purpose: Any figure that changes. The one step deliberately not on a fixed ramp: a numeral's size derives from the slot holding it.

mono.purpose: JetBrains Mono, self-hosted at build time. Measurements with units, identifiers (band, EARFCN, PCI, ICCID, IMEI), raw AT responses, log lines, copyable commands. Never a human-authored label.

shadows.name: whisper
shadows.purpose: Optional card lift in light mode. Resolves to 0 0 #0000 in dark, where the tonal step already does the work. Never load-bearing.

shadows.name: popover-float
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, dropdowns, popovers, the skip-to-content pill. The 'not part of the page flow' signal, and the one place a shadow carries real meaning.

motion.name: ease-emphasized
motion.purpose: A deliberate departure and a long settle. Container size and shape, aggregation re-proportioning, banner arrival, meter first-fill.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: The everyday state change, and the right default. Card entrance, nav indicator, chip morph, meter retarget.

motion.name: ease-quick
motion.purpose: Moves too brief to need shaping: label swaps, value ticks, hover tints, focus rings. At the short end of the scale a bespoke cubic is indistinguishable from the built-in.

motion.name: ease-ambient
motion.purpose: The two sanctioned ambient loops only, paired with alternate.

motion.name: duration-quick
motion.purpose: Label swaps, live value ticks, hover tints, focus rings.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: The default for a state change.

motion.name: duration-emphasized
motion.purpose: Container size and shape, arrival. This is the ceiling for the whole product — state the rule as the token, never as the number.

motion.name: duration-ambient
motion.purpose: The service-ring pulse and the live-ping dot. Nothing else loops. Deliberately NOT scaled with the transition tokens: a loop is not a transition.

motion.name: stagger-step
motion.purpose: The card cascade step, with a 10px rise. Wider and the last card reads as the page still loading.

motion.name: stagger-step-rows
motion.purpose: The in-card row cascade, with a 5px rise. Rows sit ~6px apart, so a 10px lift would read as the card reflowing. `rowCascadeDelay(index)` derives both this step and its ten-row cap.

motion.name: tick-stagger-step
motion.purpose: The step between two figures' dips inside one TickGroup. Not an entrance: the floor is ~1/8th of the dip, below which consecutive dips merge.

breakpoints.name: @3xl/main
breakpoints.purpose: Paired cards go side by side; the page header goes to a row.

breakpoints.name: @5xl/main
breakpoints.purpose: Summary tiles go 4-up; the three-card dashboard row goes 3-up.

breakpoints.name: desktop
breakpoints.purpose: The one named viewport breakpoint, for shell-level concerns.

toneSteps.name: tone-success
toneSteps.purpose: Per the Explicit-Tone Rule: concentric rings, halo discs, and nested tonal surfaces use these three explicit steps instead of stacked alpha, because stacked alpha compounds differently over a card than over a container tile.

toneSteps.name: tone-warning
toneSteps.purpose: Per the Explicit-Tone Rule: concentric rings, halo discs, and nested tonal surfaces use these three explicit steps instead of stacked alpha.

toneSteps.name: tone-destructive
toneSteps.purpose: Per the Explicit-Tone Rule: concentric rings, halo discs, and nested tonal surfaces use these three explicit steps instead of stacked alpha.

iconLibraries.name: Material Symbols Rounded
iconLibraries.scope: The sidebar, /dashboard, the two pre-auth routes (/ and /login/), and the entire /cellular/ family — index plus all 17 sub-routes.
iconLibraries.note: Ligature-driven and self-hosted, subset at build time from a shared glyph list. Sets fontSize as an inline style, so a parent's [&>svg]:size-3 cannot reach it — pass size explicitly at every call site. Always aria-hidden beside a real text label.

iconLibraries.name: lucide-react
iconLibraries.scope: Every other route — /local-network/, /monitoring/, /system-settings/, /about-device, /support, onboarding — plus every route-agnostic primitive (the page-level Banner, the apply-progress dialog) wherever it mounts.
iconLibraries.note: A lucide glyph on an unconverted route is correct code, not a defect, and a route-agnostic component stays on lucide even when it mounts inside a Material route, because it cannot know where it will appear. The boundary is per ROUTE, never per directory. Convert a whole route or none of it.

iconLibraries.name: react-icons/md
iconLibraries.scope: The dashboard Network Status card only.
iconLibraries.note: A sanctioned exception: '5G', '4G+' and '3G' are typographic marks Material Symbols has no equivalent for.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The main action on any surface — Record, Save, Apply. Full-round pill, 42px, brand fill.

components.name: Tonal Button
components.description: A secondary action of equal standing. The container pair, so it reads as a peer of the primary rather than a weaker copy.

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: The only correct status indicator: a role container, that container's ink, no border, pill radius, and a mandatory 12px glyph. The glyph is load-bearing — success and warning containers measure 1.03:1 apart.
components.html: Connected

components.name: Identity Chip
components.description: Says which RADIO a surface belongs to — blue for the 5G NR leg, violet for 4G LTE. Never means healthy, and is never interchangeable with a status role.

components.name: Hero Card
components.description: The anchor card on a surface: 40px radius, no border, tonal separation only, with an optional whisper shadow that is never load-bearing.
components.html:
Network Status

Registration, carrier, and link state.

components.name: Summary Tile
components.description: The inner unit of a glance surface: a 28px block, 92px tall, holding a 52px glyph disc beside eyebrow, value, and caption. The disc always INVERTS the tile's pairing so the icon pops instead of dissolving.
components.html: Bandwidth70MHz20 + 30 + 20

components.name: Metric Row Pill
components.description: The glance-surface metric row: a 40px full-round pill on surface-container, a 13px/600 muted key against a 13px tabular-nums value. The 20px line box is load-bearing — it holds the row at exactly 40px so its skeleton keeps matching.

components.name: Sidebar Nav Item (active)
components.description: One primary-container pill per group, which SLIDES between rows rather than appearing. The active row also thickens its glyph's FILL axis — an accessibility affordance, so the state survives grayscale.
components.html: Radio Information

components.name: Input Field
components.description: 20px radius, 42px tall, a surface-container fill and no visible border at rest. Focus adds a ring; the fill does not change.

components.name: Tonal Banner

narrative.overview:
QManager is the calm, expert console an operator trusts when something matters. Color is not scarce here, it is **structured**: a Material-3-style tonal palette derived from the QManager mark, where content sits *inside* filled tonal containers rather than being sprinkled as colored text on white. Density is the job; color organizes the density instead of decorating it.

The aesthetic is **tonal at rest, expressive in transition, dense in data, honest in state**. A surface tells you what kind of thing it is by its fill and its radius before you read a word of it. Nothing shouts, because everything is a container: hierarchy comes from tone, size, and shape rather than from one loud focal element competing for attention.

It earns its restraint twice. Once as a stylistic principle, and again as a safety principle: QManager is served by the modem it manages, so the routine 90% should feel effortless and the risky 10% should feel deliberate. A colorful interface is not permission to become a consumer router app.

Dominant references: **Material 3** (Pixel Settings, Google Home) for the shape scale, container roles, and motion curves; **Apple System Settings** for the uniform page-header-plus-card-grid structure; **Vercel / Linear** for light-and-dark parity and typographic restraint; **Grafana** for data-viz density; **UniFi** for inline status density — a density reference only, never a badge or layout one. Anti-references: raw terminal aesthetics, legacy router admin panels, consumer-router cartoon oversimplification, the AI/SaaS hero-metric template, and **decorative color** — a hue used because a surface looked empty.
keyCharacteristics: OKLCH only. `#000` and `#fff` never appear as literals; every neutral is tinted toward hue 258.
The palette is derived from the mark, not chosen alongside it.
Three identity hues (blue, violet, cyan) plus the functional four. No hue is decorative and functional at the same time.
Rethink Sans is the interface voice; JetBrains Mono is the machine voice. There is no third.
Depth is tonal. Shadows exist, are optional, and are never load-bearing.
Motion is expressive in duration and curve, capped at `emphasized`, and never overshoots.
Light and dark are first-class equals; dark mode is genuinely colored, not desaturated.
Responsive behavior is driven by container queries, not viewport breakpoints.
No runtime asset fetches. Fonts and the icon font are self-hosted and subset at build time — the modem may have no internet.
Build on shadcn/ui first, restyled with these tokens. Build custom only where shadcn has no answer.

rules.name: The Source-Color Rule
rules.body: Every new color derives from the mark's hue family or from an existing identity or functional role. Nobody picks a hue by eye and adds it to `globals.css`.

rules.name: The Container-Pair Rule
rules.body: A fill takes its own `-foreground`; a container takes its own `on-` ink. Never cross them. Crossing a fill with a container's ink is the single most common way to fail contrast here, and it is often invisible in light mode while breaking dark.

rules.name: The Paired-Theme Rule
rules.body: A role's fill and its ink move together across themes. Dark-mode fills are light (L 0.77-0.87), so their inks flip dark (L 0.22-0.24). Raising a dark fill without flipping its ink is what kept destructive measuring 2.42:1 through three migration steps. An alpha on a fill (`bg-destructive/60`) is a request to the canvas, not to the token, so the same control renders a different color in a card, a dialog, and a popover — never compensate with one.

rules.name: The 40-Degree Rule
rules.body: No decorative hue sits within 40 degrees of a functional one. Identity hues occupy 264 / 296 / 200; functional hues occupy 149 / 72 / 27 plus the brand ramp.

rules.name: The Info-Is-Brand Rule
rules.body: There is no separate info hue. "In progress" renders as the brand's own tonal container, so an informational chip and a primary button differ by shape and glyph (pill plus clock vs. filled button plus label), never by owning two different blues.

rules.name: The Identity-Never-Acts Rule
rules.body: Carrier Violet and Uplink Cyan carry identity, never affordance. A violet surface is never clickable *because* it is violet, and no control is ever tinted by them. The corollary: `nr` and `lte` never mean "healthy".

rules.name: The Explicit-Tone Rule
rules.body: Layered translucency is banned for stacked shapes. Concentric rings, halo discs, and nested tonal surfaces use the explicit `--tone-{role}-{1,2,3}` steps, because stacked alpha compounds differently over each surface and yields a different color in a card than in a dialog.

rules.name: The Functional-Color Promise
rules.body: A user who learns green means healthy on the dashboard finds the same green meaning the same thing in Watchdog, in Profile Apply, and in the alert logs. Hues get retuned; meanings never move.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Rethink Sans is the interface, JetBrains Mono is the machine. There is no third typeface. Pairing Rethink Sans with another UI sans (Inter, Geist Sans, IBM Plex, Roboto, Manrope) is forbidden.

rules.name: The Machine-Voice Rule
rules.body: `font-mono` is scoped to machine truth that is not itself a changing figure: identifiers (band, EARFCN, PCI, ICCID, IMEI, MAC/IP addresses), static facts read back from config rather than sampled live (a band's reference bandwidth in a disclosure table, a resolved timezone offset, a fixed scoring weight), raw AT responses, log lines, and copyable commands. A human-authored label never wears it. A live measurement — RSRP, throughput, a countdown, a ticking relative-time caption — is the interface reporting a number rather than the machine's raw output, so it takes `--font-sans` and `tabular-nums` instead of `font-mono`. A count is a changing figure and stays `font-sans`; a nav item is neither and gets no font-family override at all.

rules.name: The Weight-Discipline Rule
rules.body: 400 body, 500 labels and medium emphasis, 600 headings and numerics, 700 page titles only.

rules.name: The Tabular-Number Rule
rules.body: Any figure that can change while on screen is `tabular-nums`, in whichever voice it's already in — a live measurement keeps `tabular-nums` in `font-sans`, and an identifier column that needs vertical alignment keeps it in `font-mono`. The class controls digit-width jitter; it does not decide which voice owns the value. A latency readout whose digits shift width reads as the layout twitching, not as the value moving — and a tonal pill makes that jitter more visible, not less.

rules.name: The Truncation-Pair Rule
rules.body: Where two cards sit side by side as a pair, every text node in their headers carries `min-w-0` and `truncate`. One card wrapping to two lines while its sibling stays at one breaks the paired baseline, and the pair stops reading as a pair. Italian is the locale that trips it.

rules.name: The Consistent-Layout Rule
rules.body: Page header plus a uniform card grid, on every feature page. A bespoke hero-driven layout invented for a single screen is a consistency failure even when it looks good in isolation. A genuine glance surface may earn a hero card; it is a rare exception, never the default.

rules.name: The Card-Wrapped Surface Rule
rules.body: The unit of composition is the card that wraps a settings group, not the page. The card owns its whole content (`CardHeader` plus `CardContent` with every control); the page only arranges cards. A feature that scatters loose fragments across the viewport has skipped the card.

rules.name: The Container-Query Rule
rules.body: New responsive behavior is a container query against `@container/main` or a card-local `@container/card`. Reach for a viewport breakpoint only for the page gutter or the shell itself.

rules.name: The Tonal-Elevation Rule
rules.body: Two surfaces at different conceptual elevations differ by at least one container step. If two surfaces are only distinguishable by their shadow, one of them is on the wrong step of the ramp.

rules.name: The No-Hairline-On-Fill Rule
rules.body: A tonal container never also carries a border. Cards on converted surfaces ship `border-0` explicitly, because a hairline over a fill reads as chrome around the color rather than as the edge of a block. `--outline` is for input strokes and genuine table rules only.

rules.name: The Highlight-by-Container Rule
rules.body: Emphasis promotes a surface one container step and changes its ink, rather than adding a translucent wash over a neutral card. A recommended alignment slot becomes a `primary-container` block; a running pipeline step becomes a `primary-container` row.

rules.name: The Radius-Follows-Size Rule
rules.body: A surface's radius is a function of its size and role, not of taste. A 28px tile never sits inside a 20px field, and a banner never out-rounds the card it sits on.

rules.name: The Fill-Over-Stroke Rule
rules.body: When a shape needs to be distinguished from its neighbor, change its fill, not its border. This system has one stroke color and it is for inputs and table rules.

rules.name: The Role-Radius Rule
rules.body: New work uses the role scale above. The legacy `rounded-{sm,md,lg,xl}` chain off `--radius: 0.65rem` still resolves for ~349 unconverted call sites and keeps its old values, but it is never the correct choice in a new component.

rules.name: The Motion-Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Nothing exceeds `emphasized` (800ms), and `emphasized` is the ceiling, not a starting point. State the rule as *the token*, never as the number — the number moved once already and every place it had been written out longhand had to be hunted down.

rules.name: The One-Scale Rule
rules.body: A duration in a component is a bug. Every transition reads `duration-[var(--duration-standard)]` (or `-quick` / `-emphasized`) in a className, or `DUR.standard` (etc.) in a `motion/react` transition; a bare `duration-200`, an inline `{ duration: 0.25 }`, or a `transition-all` with no duration at all (which silently inherits Tailwind's 150ms) is off the scale and will not retune with it. The exceptions are narrow and each carries a comment: continuous loops with their own tempo (spinners, the OTP caret) and linear data-driven progress bars. `{ duration: 0 }` as a reduced-motion escape is always fine.

rules.name: The Non-Load-Bearing Rule
rules.body: If a transition never runs — reduced motion, a backgrounded tab, a paint that beat the animation — the UI must already be correct. Every entrance keyframe in `globals.css` is written open-ended (`from` with no `to`) for exactly this reason: the resting value is the truth and the keyframe only describes the journey. A `requestAnimationFrame`-armed state flip breaks this rule, because rAF does not fire in a background tab.

rules.name: The Transform-Only Rule
rules.body: Animate `transform` and `opacity`. The single sanctioned `width` animation in the product is the carrier-aggregation segment, where the width *is* the data and a `scaleX` would distort the band labels riding inside it. Meters animate `scaleX`, never `width` — on a CPU also carrying the user's traffic, a per-poll layout pass per meter is not free.

rules.name: The One-Loop Rule
rules.body: At most one ambient loop per surface, and only where something is genuinely live. Two exist product-wide: the service-ring pulse and the live-ping dot.

rules.name: The No-Overshoot Rule
rules.body: Never springy, never elastic, never rubber-banding. The one sanctioned overshoot in the entire product is the save-confirmation check at 1.03 scale — and it is a **number**, not a sentence: `SAVE_CHECK_OVERSHOOT` / `SAVE_CHECK_KEYFRAMES` / `transitionSaveCheck` in `lib/motion.ts`. Anything that wants the pop imports the constant; a second overshoot has to be written out in the open to exist. This rule and that file both cited the save check as the sanctioned exception while the button underneath was running an underdamped spring (`stiffness: 400, damping: 22`) whose peak is a function of its two dials and is bounded by nothing — a ceiling enforced only by prose is not a ceiling.

rules.name: The Enter-Only Rule
rules.body: Conditions and navigation have no exit animation. A banner leaving means the condition cleared and that should feel immediate; an outgoing route is already gone, and animating it out only delays the incoming one.

rules.name: The Modal-Exit Rule
rules.body: A modal's exit duration is an **input-latency budget**, not a taste call, and every modal surface therefore writes its two directions separately: `data-[state=open]:` on `emphasized`, `data-[state=closed]:` on `quick`. Never one unqualified `duration-*` for both. The reason is mechanical rather than aesthetic: Radix sets `pointer-events: none` on `<body>` for as long as a modal layer is mounted and releases it in an unmount cleanup, and `<Presence>` holds that layer mounted until `animationend` fires on the content node — so the entire page is click-dead for exactly the length of the exit animation. Two consequences, each violated on its own: the scrim shares the content's clock in **both** directions (an overlay with no duration is a One-Scale violation and the thing that turns a slow exit into an apparently broken one), and `quick` is the ceiling for a modal exit, not a suggestion (distance does not buy budget — a sheet travels a full viewport edge and still exits on `quick`).

rules.name: The Filled-Chip Rule
rules.body: Status chips are a role container plus that container's ink, no border, pill radius, always an icon. `variant="outline"` is never a status indicator.

rules.name: The Every-Chip-Has-A-Glyph Rule
rules.body: `success-container` and `warning-container` measure 1.03:1 apart — the same surface to the eye, and identical under deuteranopia. The glyph is the only thing separating healthy from degraded. Two states in the same slot must never share a glyph either.

rules.name: The Identity-Chip Rule
rules.body: Where a chip's fill carries identity, the quality it *also* reports must be encoded non-chromatically. On the signal cards that channel is the Material glyph's bar count.

rules.name: The Glyph-Disc Rule
rules.body: A state icon sits in a filled circle on the role's strong fill. The disc is what survives when the container fill washes out in sunlight; a bare glyph on the container does not.

rules.name: The Skeleton-Mirror Rule
rules.body: A skeleton mirrors the loaded geometry by importing the same shape constant, never by restating numbers.

rules.name: The Loader-and-Dots Rule
rules.body: Step or sample progress is a `Loader2Icon` spinner plus dot indicators. Fill and progress bars are reserved for data visualization — signal strength, quality meters, bandwidth share.

rules.name: The Age-Gated Tone Rule
rules.body: On a surface listing *history*, two independent axes decide how a row is drawn. Tone is what kind of thing happened; it is a fact about the event, never expires, and is carried by a filled icon disc in the solid role color for as long as the row exists. Weight is how much the row still deserves attention, and it does expire: a row keeps its tonal container while it is fresh (one hour) or unresolved, then settles onto `surface-container` with its disc at full strength. The disc never consults the age gate — an hour-old recovery sits on a plain surface with its green check still green, and a still-standing outage never greys out merely because time passed. Note that `severity: "info"` here means *routine*, not *good*.

rules.name: The Dismiss-Only-Notices Rule
rules.body: A banner gets an X only when it is a *notification*. A standing condition has no dismiss, because dismissing it would hide a fact that is still true.

rules.name: The State-Honesty Rule
rules.body: A status surface reports what is actually running — saved settings, live service state — never the half-edited form. A control that cannot currently work explains why instead of sitting there dead. A test only runs against saved config. An ambient animation only loops where something is genuinely live.

rules.name: The No-Dot-Separator Rule
rules.body: A meta line joining two or more short facts (`PCI 135`, `EARFCN 9485`) uses plain spacing, never a `·` glue character — dots read as sloppy filler, not structure. Give the facts room (multiple spaces, or separate flex/inline items with a gap) instead of punctuating between them.

dos: Do pick a pair — a fill with its own `-foreground`, or a container with its own `on-` ink.
Do give every status chip an icon, and give two states in the same slot two different icons.
Do use `--chart-nr` and `--chart-lte` for series color; one hue per radio family.
Do reach for the role radii (`rounded-tile` / `card` / `hero` / `pill`) in new work.
Do ship `border-0` on a card and let the tone step carry the separation.
Do write responsive behavior as a container query against `@container/main`.
Do wrap a settings group in a card and let the page arrange cards.
Do put `min-w-0 truncate` on every text node in a paired card's header.
Do mark every changing figure `tabular-nums` in the interface font; reserve `font-mono` for identifiers and raw machine strings.
Do mirror a skeleton's geometry from the same exported shape constant the loaded view uses.
Do build the loading, empty, and error state in the same change as the loaded one.
Do pass `size` explicitly at every `MaterialSymbol` call site.
Do keep interactive targets at 44px on coarse pointers, and let toolbars wrap.
Do make a status surface report *saved* state, and make an incapable control explain itself.
Do defer anything that reboots the modem behind a dialog plus a persistent banner.
Do key every new user-visible string across all five locales; `bun run i18n:check` gates it.
donts: Don't put ink from one role on another role's surface, or a container's ink on a fill.
Don't hardcode `text-white` on a destructive fill — in dark mode that fill is *light*.
Don't compensate for a mismatched pair with an alpha (`bg-destructive/60`); fix the pair.
Don't use `variant="outline"` as a status indicator.
Don't use `nr` or `lte` to mean "healthy", or tint a control with an identity hue.
Don't use the numbered `--chart-1..6`; they do not theme.
Don't stack alpha to build concentric shapes — use the explicit `--tone-{role}-{1,2,3}` steps.
Don't put a border on a tonal container, or use `--outline` as a card edge.
Don't animate `width` (the aggregation segment is the sole exception) or exceed `emphasized`.
Don't write a raw duration (`duration-200`, `{ duration: 0.25 }`) or a `transition-all` with no duration — see The One-Scale Rule.
Don't add a third stagger step, a fifth duration, or a spring.
Don't add an exit animation to a banner or a route transition.
Don't give a modal one unqualified `duration-*` for both directions, or leave its scrim without one — the exit clock is how long the page stays click-dead. See The Modal-Exit Rule.
Don't loop an animation where nothing is genuinely live.
Don't put an icon in a `CardHeader`.
Don't invent a bespoke hero-driven layout for one screen.
